newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine guerrilla sentenced to life in prison.
newsitem.headline: Argentine guerrilla sentenced to life in prison.

text.p: An Argentine court sentenced leftist guerrilla Enrique Gorriaran Merlo to life in prison on Thursday for a 1989 attack on an army barracks that killed 39 people.
His ex-wife, Ana Sivori, accused of being an accomplice in the attack, was sentenced to 18 years in jail.

Gorriaran, 55, for years was one of Latin America's most wanted men and has admitted killing former Nicaraguan dictator Anastasio Somoza while he was in exile in Paraguay. He sat silently as the verdict was read, but Sivori shouted: "This is the justice we have. Filthy justice!"
Prosecutors on Wednesday demanded life sentences for Gorriaran and Sivori. Argentine law permits lifers to apply for release after 25 years. Sivori could go free after eight years in jail.
Gorriaran showed no remorse and during his own defence late on Wednesday asked for the maximum possible sentence.

"Given the characteristics of this tribunal it would be humiliating if they did not give me the highest possible sentence," he said. "I am not going to join the indecent wave of repentant guerrillas."

Gorriaran and Sivori fired their lawyers a week ago saying they were already condemned. They spent three hours on Wednesday justifying their actions before a court judging them for the country's last major guerrilla action, in which 39 people died, 60 were wounded and three were reported missing.

They contrasted their trial with the amnesty declared in 1989 for military personnel who took part in the 1970s "Dirty War" in which at least 10,000 Argentines "disappeared" at the hands of death squads.
"If I were someone who disappeared people, or a torturer or a murderer, I would have been pardoned," Gorriaran said. Sivori added: "If I were the wife of a soldier none of this would be happening."

Gorriaran was arrested while walking down a street in Mexico after years on the run. He alleges he was kidnapped by Mexican and Argentine secret servicemen and taken to Argentina illegally without extradition proceedings.
He founded the Marxist People's Revolutionary Army (ERP), which carried out many bloody attacks and kidnappings in the 1970s. Later he founded the All for the Fatherland Movement (MTP).

He admitted in a clandestine television interview before his capture that he planned and carried out the assassination of Somoza in Paraguay in 1980. He also argued that he carried out the assault on the Argentine army's La Tablada barracks to head off a threatened coup against the elected government of then-President Raul Alfonsin.
